proposed_comments.title: Preserve explicit fallback disable and notify dependent flags
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: One coordinated normalization/notification correction plus two persistence/notification regressions spans separated Update locations and the test file; the prompt specifies the tested localized changes together rather than exposing a partial condition-only correction.
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve explicit fallback disable and notify dependent flags

**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/FallbackSettingsViewModel.cs:Update` (lines 84-103), its `IsEnabled`/`IncludeInGlobalResults` setters, and their bindings in `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Settings/ExtensionPage.xaml`. Regression tests belong in `src/modules/cmdpal/Tests/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.UnitTests/ProviderFallbackSettingsTests.cs`.

**Problem:** Starting with both flags `true`, setting `IsEnabled = false` enters this normalization branch and sets it back to `true`. The normalized record then equals the existing record, so the method returns without saving or notifying. The refactor therefore makes the off switch ineffective for a fallback included in global results; the previous setter explicitly cleared global inclusion on disable.

**Why it matters:** Users cannot disable these fallbacks through the setting. In the opposite transition, setting global inclusion on a disabled fallback changes both flags but notifies only `IncludeInGlobalResults`, leaving `IsEnabled` bindings without the dependent update.

**Suggested change:**
1. Keep this centralized update method, but let an explicit disable win. Add `propertyName != nameof(IsEnabled)` to the enable-normalization condition so the following branch can clear `IncludeInGlobalResults` when the user turns the fallback off.
2. Capture the previous record before replacing `_fallbackSettings`; after the existing notification, notify each of `IsEnabled` and `IncludeInGlobalResults` whose value changed and whose name is not already `propertyName`.
3. Persist the normalized record once and retain the existing single reload message. Add the two transition regressions to `ProviderFallbackSettingsTests`, asserting persisted flags, exactly one write and notifications for both changed properties.

**Verification:** The exact original view-model reproduced an ignored disable with zero writes/notifications and an inclusion transition missing the dependent notification. The localized correction built successfully and all ten focused fallback-settings tests passed, including new regressions verifying persisted flags and both notifications. Add those two transition regressions to `ProviderFallbackSettingsTests`, retain the existing defaults/persistence tests, and verify the settings toggle and checkbox stay consistent interactively.
